catalogue.title: School closure reversals: evidence for Kew Riverside Primary School
catalogue.scope: A purposive catalogue of 12 English state-funded primary schools with a documented stopped closure or merger proposal, 2019-2026, alongside four selected closure comparisons. These cases are not a national census, a representative sample or a matched control group. They cannot estimate a survival rate or the effectiveness of a campaign tactic.
catalogue.unit: School for catalogue and stage counts; grouped decision episode for the reasons matrix.

schools.name: Fletching Church of England Primary School
schools.reason: The council's recommendation relied on an improved short-term budget, a largely maintained roll and the diocese's position. Its subsequent admissions report confirms that closure did not proceed.
schools.lesson: Give the council a revised budget with evidenced funding and realistic pupil assumptions.
schools.limit: The council still expected recurring deficits and did not validate long-term recovery.
schools.transfer: Useful financial example; rural context differs from Kew.

schools.name: Godshill Primary School
schools.reason: Cabinet retained the school, citing community interests, the rural-school presumption and earlier decisions concerning Chillerton and Godshill.
schools.lesson: Link community evidence to the decision criteria and to the council's past commitments.
schools.limit: The rural-school protection does not automatically apply to Kew Riverside Primary School.
schools.locator: December Cabinet outcome; S04 response explaining Godshill's removal
schools.transfer: Same community-school type, but the rural setting limits the comparison.

schools.name: Brading Church of England Controlled Primary School
schools.reason: Cabinet voted not to proceed. Published minutes record scrutiny and questions about costs and data, but do not isolate the reason for this school's outcome.
schools.lesson: Prepare evidence that members can use in scrutiny and the final decision.
schools.limit: A campaign's presence does not establish that it caused the vote.
schools.transfer: Relevant decision-making example; linked to the same local programme as four other entries.

schools.name: Oakfield Church of England Aided Primary School, Ryde
schools.reason: Cabinet voted not to proceed. The minutes document the outcome without a school-specific causal explanation.
schools.lesson: Use a clear evidence brief as well as taking part formally.
schools.limit: It shares a Cabinet episode with Brading and Wroxall, so it does not count as a separate, independent result.
schools.locator: S05 Cabinet item 101a; S06 account of the diocesan challenge
schools.transfer: The faith-school context differs, but preparing evidence is still relevant.

schools.name: Wroxall Primary School
schools.reason: Cabinet voted not to proceed. The minutes do not attribute that decision to a particular intervention.
schools.lesson: Find out what evidence decision-makers need before the vote.
schools.limit: The council said further school-place reviews would still be needed.
schools.transfer: Same community-school type, but the island-wide context differs.

schools.name: Arreton St George's Church of England (Aided) Primary School
schools.reason: The adjudicators rejected the proposal because significant procedural flaws could have affected the outcome and the rural community impact had not been properly considered.
schools.lesson: Audit the selection method, evidence and community-impact assessment.
schools.limit: The ruling stopped this proposal. It did not show permanent financial viability.
schools.transfer: The lessons on evidence are relevant, but referral rights and rural status need separate checks.

schools.name: St John the Divine Church of England Primary School
schools.reason: The adjudicator found deficiencies in the process and insufficient evidence that pupil transfers would produce a sustainable receiving school.
schools.lesson: Test what families actually prefer and the financial effects of pupils moving.
schools.limit: Mixed-age classes were discussed as a possible option, not an approved recovery plan. Long-term sustainability remained uncertain.
schools.transfer: A strong London example on demand and cost, but its governance differs from Kew.

schools.name: Fenstanton Primary School
schools.reason: The adjudicators rejected the closure and related amalgamation proposals because the decisions and procedures were unlawful.
schools.lesson: Keep a dated record of proposals, conditions, decisions and who has authority to make them.
schools.limit: The alternative merger was also rejected. The result did not validate its business case or establish a general parental appeal right.
schools.transfer: London community school, but part of linked proposals with a faith school.

schools.name: Holy Trinity Church of England Primary School, Tulse Hill
schools.reason: The same adjudication left both Holy Trinity and Fenstanton open after rejecting the linked proposals.
schools.lesson: Check the process and who has authority to decide, as well as any alternative proposal.
schools.limit: This is one shared adjudication with Fenstanton, not a second independent success.
schools.transfer: London financial pressures are relevant, but the school type and linked proposal differ.

schools.name: Pooles Park Primary School
schools.reason: The minister retained the academy order. The recorded rationale was a willing sponsor, a viable academy model and additional SEND provision and community benefits.
schools.lesson: An alternative needs a capable organisation willing to deliver it.
schools.limit: The school changed governance. Its academy-order circumstances cannot be assumed for Kew.
schools.locator: 2024 High Court judgment, paragraphs 1 and 52-53; GIAS successor URN 150522
schools.current_status: Academy successor open in GIAS on 22 September 2026
schools.transfer: London example of a deliverable alternative, with materially different statutory circumstances.

schools.name: St George's Church of England Primary School, Langton Matravers
schools.reason: News reports quote the trust ending consultation following feedback and ruling out structural changes in 2026/27 and 2027/28.
schools.lesson: Use early consultation to expose unanswered questions and seek a clear written response.
schools.limit: The outcome relies on news reports that quote the trust. Objections about process are not independent findings that anything was unlawful. Long-term options were still under review.
schools.transfer: Early-stage example; academy and rural setting differ.

schools.name: Hazlewood Community Primary School
schools.type_at_decision: Foundation (GIAS); OSA landing page labels community
schools.outcome: Merger rejected; renewed closure proposal reported
schools.reason: The adjudicator rejected the proposed merger but found that, without replacement-building capital, the school should eventually close.
schools.lesson: A reprieve on process grounds needs a plan for the underlying capital or running-cost problem.
schools.limit: A renewed closure proposal was reported on 15 September 2026. This has not been shown to be a lasting turnaround.
schools.locator: STP663, paragraphs 67-74; BBC syndicated report 15 September 2026
schools.current_status: Open in GIAS on 22 September 2026; renewed proposal reported
schools.transfer: A useful warning about whether a reprieve lasts; its major building issues differ from Kew.

comparison.name: Cowes Primary School
comparison.note: Included to complete the original six-school 2024 Isle of Wight closure cohort, not in the 12 reprieve cases.

reason_episodes.label: Fletching
reason_episodes.note: Recommendation expressly cites improved budget, stable roll and diocesan position (7.3). Community/rural issues were considered; they are not isolated as decisive in 7.3.

reason_episodes.label: Godshill
reason_episodes.note: Council explanation cites community, rural presumption and earlier local decisions.

reason_episodes.label: Brading / Oakfield / Wroxall
reason_episodes.note: Issues appear in the wider proceedings and diocesan account. Minutes do not explain why these three specific votes went against closure. No grounds are coded 2.

reason_episodes.label: Arreton St George's
reason_episodes.note: STP661 explicitly links significant procedural/evidential flaws and unassessed rural-community impact to rejection. Diocese made the referral.

reason_episodes.label: St John the Divine
reason_episodes.note: STP659 paragraph 61 states process deficiencies and failure to demonstrate the receiving school's sustainability. Mixed-age organisation and community services were discussed but not necessary to the conclusion.

reason_episodes.label: Fenstanton / Holy Trinity
reason_episodes.note: STP662 rejects both proposals on procedural and jurisdictional grounds. Merger budget/alternative was not validated; diocesan referral provided the route.

reason_episodes.label: Pooles Park
reason_episodes.note: Minister's recorded rationale includes viability assessment, a strong sponsor and SEND/community benefits (judgment 52-53).

reason_episodes.label: St George's, Langton
reason_episodes.note: Secondary reports record feedback and objections. No independently examined decision rationale, so no factor is coded 2.

reason_episodes.label: Hazlewood
reason_episodes.note: Proposed mechanism could not create the intended merged school. Capital difficulties remained; future closure was contemplated (67-74).

coding.0: Not established in the reviewed record. Does not mean absent.
coding.1: Raised, considered or part of the route; not established as a ground for the favourable outcome.
coding.2: Expressly supported as part of the decision/recommendation rationale. Does not prove causal effectiveness.

fletching_budget.measure: Forecast year-end balance, as reported in December 2019; not outturn
fletching_budget.note: The third-year range reflects different pupil assumptions. The full budget change is not attributable to fundraising alone.

priorities.deliverable: Three-year budget; staffing and class options; low, central and high pupil scenarios; confirmed bridge funding and delivery partner.
priorities.evidence: Fletching; Pooles Park; St John the Divine
priorities.why: Provides an implementable alternative and exposes the recurring funding gap.

priorities.work: Audit demand and the net saving
priorities.deliverable: Traceable pupil forecasts, family destination evidence, transition costs and continuing building/PFI costs.
priorities.why: Tests whether closure would achieve the benefits used to justify it.

priorities.deliverable: Aggregated evidence on journeys, SEND continuity, nursery/community use and parental preferences; no public personal data.
priorities.why: Makes community effects concrete and relevant to the decision.

priorities.deliverable: Concise consultation submission with numbered evidence, costed alternatives and questions that need answers; work with governors.
priorities.why: Gives the decision-maker usable material before the next stage.

priorities.deliverable: Dated decision log and specific concerns about process; check whether the school type is eligible before relying on a referral route.
priorities.why: Can expose a defective proposal, but a reprieve may leave the underlying problem unresolved.

comparisons.definition: Selected cases in which documented efforts did not prevent the named school's closure. This does not mean the effort had no benefit. St Bartholomew's obtained a transition extension. These four cases are not a representative or statistically matched control group.

schools.name: Cowes Primary School
schools.outcome: Closure approved by Cabinet; GIAS confirms closure on 31 August 2025.

efforts.text: An online petition to save the school had 479 signatures in the council's reported initial-consultation snapshot.
The local councillor spoke on behalf of Cowes Primary at the Cabinet meeting before leaving the room for the decision.

schools.reason: The statutory notice cited declining pupil numbers at Cowes and significant surplus places in its planning area. Cabinet approved closure. The minutes do not establish the marginal effect of the petition or the councillor's intervention.
schools.lesson: Public campaigning and political representation do not, on their own, show that the case on school places has changed. Link support to verifiable demand, costs and a deliverable alternative.
schools.comparison: Same initial six-school programme as Godshill, Brading, Oakfield, Wroxall and Arreton. This comparison gives context; it is not a controlled experiment.
schools.partial_benefit: The reviewed sources do not show any specific concession that can be credited to these efforts.
schools.limit: The signature count is a historical report snapshot, not the final campaign total or a count of affected families. No conclusion about what would have happened without the campaign is possible.
schools.locator: S05 item 101a; S27 paragraph 92; S29 paragraphs 2-3; S28 action taken; G12 closure date

schools.name: Broad Oak Community Primary School
schools.outcome: March 2020 report recommended closure after examining the governors' alternative; GIAS confirms closure on 31 August 2020.

efforts.text: Governors submitted a plan for two classes, restructured leadership and a pooled three-school federation budget.
The plan sought to build enrolment from 40-plus to 70-plus pupils during the next academic year.

schools.reason: The council's report found the pooled budget would still reach a £33,894 deficit in 2021/22. It questioned leadership capacity, absence cover and contingency, and regarded the extra-pupil target as insufficiently evidenced.
schools.lesson: Stress-test an alternative at both school and partner level: pupil recruitment, staffing, reserves, absence cover and the later years all need evidence.
schools.comparison: Same authority and rural-school review period as Fletching. Fletching's proposal stopped in December 2019; Broad Oak's plan was assessed later and closure proceeded. The cases differ in finances, school type and education concerns.
schools.partial_benefit: The governors' plan received a documented assessment of its finances and operations. This does not prove any concession on the outcome.
schools.limit: The report gives the council's assessment of the alternative, not an independent forecast audit. Its concerns must not be recast as proof that federation or mixed-age teaching generally fails.

schools.name: St Bartholomew's CofE Primary School
schools.outcome: Adjudicators approved closure with a one-term extension, from 31 August to 31 December 2024. GIAS confirms the later closure date.

efforts.text: The school proposed reducing its admission number to 20 with staffing changes, and raised federation and phased closure as alternatives.
Governors referred the decision to the adjudicator. The school and diocese argued for more time to support vulnerable pupils' transition.

schools.reason: The adjudicators accepted the demographic need to reduce places and considered the deficit, low pupil numbers and concerns over a smaller school's delivery. They found the transition arrangements insufficiently developed for some vulnerable children and extended the timetable.
schools.lesson: A challenge may improve transition without preserving the school. Keep the case for a sustainable school and the case for protecting children during any transition explicit.
schools.comparison: The same broad route, external adjudication, led to rejection at St John the Divine and to approval with a one-term extension here. The evidence and circumstances differed, so the difference cannot be put down to campaign quality.
schools.partial_benefit: One extra school term for transition, explicitly justified by the adjudicators. This is a meaningful concession, not a lasting reprieve.
schools.limit: The determination records the school as saying the diocese did not wish to pursue federation. Do not describe an agreed or funded federation as having been tested and failed.
schools.locator: S23 paragraphs 2-3, 47-49 and 79-91; G14 closure date

schools.name: De Beauvoir Primary School
schools.outcome: Cabinet agreed closure in December 2023; GIAS confirms closure on 31 August 2024.

efforts.text: Consultation produced alternative merger pairings involving De Beauvoir, including Randal Cremer and Princess May.
Across the whole Hackney package, 95% of responses that could be clearly assessed opposed the proposals. This is a programme-wide figure, not a De Beauvoir-only result.
efforts.locator: Paragraph beginning 'At the end of the consultation period'

schools.reason: The council rejected suggested pairings on grounds including walking distance and whether pupil numbers would stabilise. It maintained that the underlying demand and sustainability problem remained despite extensive opposition.
schools.lesson: Set out a willing partner, viable combined rolls and a workable site and journey plan. Treat consultation support as evidence to go with that plan, not a vote that decides closure.
schools.comparison: An urban community-school closure offers context for Kew. It is not matched on school finances, local geography or pupil demand.
schools.partial_benefit: The reviewed sources do not show any specific reprieve or transition concession that can be credited to these submissions.
schools.limit: The 95% figure is neither a representative public-opinion poll nor a school-specific percentage. The council's objections to these particular mergers do not show that all partnership options fail. S25 section 4.27 gives 207 opposed and 12 supportive proposal-level responses (219 clear responses, from a process receiving 175 submissions). A respondent could comment on several proposals; these are not 219 unique people.
schools.locator: S25 sections 4.24-4.28 and 7.10-7.15; S26 overview of decision; S30 consultation summary; G15 closure date

petition_snapshot.period: Initial consultation in autumn 2024, as reported to Cabinet on 20 March 2025
petition_snapshot.unit: Online signatures, as reported; paper signatures shown separately and not added
petition_snapshot.note: All six original proposals are included. Counts are not adjusted for school size, campaign duration, duplicate participation or signatory residence. Outcomes do not identify a petition's causal effect.

comparison_lessons.theme: An alternative must withstand financial scrutiny
comparison_lessons.record: Fletching’s short-term budget improved with largely one-off support. Its roll and the diocese’s position also supported the recommendation. Broad Oak’s revised federation budget still forecast a deficit, with concerns about leadership cover and pupil recruitment.
comparison_lessons.limit: Fletching still expected recurring deficits, so the reprieve did not show long-term recovery. It is a rural school, unlike Kew.
comparison_lessons.question: Does the alternative work across every forecast year, with credible staffing, pupil demand and partner commitments?

comparison_lessons.theme: A challenge can change a decision—or improve transition

outcomes.text: Closure approved, with an extra term for transition; closed in December 2024.

comparison_lessons.record: St John’s decision found process deficiencies. It also found too little evidence that pupil transfers would sustain the receiving school. St Bartholomew’s decision accepted closure but required more time for vulnerable pupils’ transition.
comparison_lessons.limit: A delay is a different outcome from a reprieve. These faith-school referral routes are not an automatic right of appeal for Kew parents.
comparison_lessons.question: What specific concern needs checking, and what remedy would address it?

outcomes.text: Also had a petition; closed in August 2025.

comparison_lessons.record: Petitions were recorded for all six schools. The records do not measure their effect or show a winning signature threshold.
comparison_lessons.limit: These schools were part of one local programme. The minutes do not give separate reasons for the Brading, Oakfield and Wroxall decisions.
comparison_lessons.question: Could community support help find useful evidence, relevant expertise or credible commitments?

hackney_consultation.note: Rounded 207/219. Multiple proposals could be addressed by a single respondent. Not a De Beauvoir-only percentage.

methodology:
# Methodology and interpretation

Research cutoff: 22 September 2026. Version 2.0.

This selection cannot show a national survival rate or the chance that Kew Riverside Primary School stays open.

## What this catalogue contains

The catalogue covers twelve selected English state-funded primary schools. In each, a proposed closure or site merger stopped, or provision continued through an academy successor, in decisions between December 2019 and June 2026. All twelve successor/current URNs were checked directly against the Department for Education's Get Information about Schools (GIAS) register on 22 September 2026. All were listed open. Hazlewood has a renewed closure proposal reported in September 2026. An open register entry does not prove a sustainable budget, enrolment recovery or protection against a future proposal.

Four more closure comparisons are included: Cowes, Broad Oak, St Bartholomew's and De Beauvoir. All four closure dates were checked directly in GIAS. Cowes also completes the original six-school 2024 Isle of Wight programme. It is counted only once among the sixteen named schools and is not counted among the twelve reprieves.

The comparison cases were chosen after the reprieve research. Broad Oak and Cowes link to authorities/programmes already covered. St Bartholomew's gives a different adjudication outcome, and De Beauvoir an urban community-school comparison. These comparisons were chosen on purpose to give context. They are not a matched control group or a complete set of unsuccessful campaigns. Adding them does not remove selection bias.

“Did not prevent closure” describes the observed outcome in a case where an effort is documented. It does not establish that the effort was useless or that it reduced the chance of success. St Bartholomew's secured an explicitly reasoned extra term for transition. Other benefits, counterfactual outcomes, total campaign spending and effort intensity are not measured. Council assessments are attributed, not presented as independently audited findings.

## Selection and searches

Targeted searches used terms including primary school closure withdrawn, rejected, not to proceed, saved from closure and scrapped. Searches were refined to named schools, councils, dioceses, official adjudicator decisions and follow-up records. London cases and cases illustrating the initial consultation stage were prioritised. Council records and OSA determinations were preferred over campaign accounts. This is a purposive search, not a registered systematic review and not a census of every eligible school.

England was selected because Kew Riverside Primary School is an English maintained community school. Independent schools, Scottish/Welsh/Northern Irish schools, mothballed schools and academic-performance turnarounds are not pooled into the analytical set. A news report describing a school as saved is not itself evidence of a lasting recovery. St George's, Langton is retained as an explicitly labelled reporting-based case because it is a recent early-stage withdrawal.

## Units and denominators

- Exhibit 1: 12 schools. Initial consultation 3; local decision after statutory notice 3; external intervention 6. An academy consultation is grouped by broad stage, not claimed to be the identical statutory process.
- Exhibit 2: 9 grouped decision episodes. Fenstanton and Holy Trinity share one adjudication. Brading, Oakfield and Wroxall share one Cabinet episode. These groups reduce obvious duplication, but other Isle of Wight and Lambeth episodes remain related.
- Exhibit 3: all 6 original schools in one named local programme. One removed before statutory notice, three retained by Cabinet, one retained after adjudication and Cowes closed on 31 August 2025. This denominator is defined locally; it is not representative of national proposals.
- Exhibit 4: a single school's contemporaneous financial forecasts, in pounds. These are forecast year-end balances, not annual funding needs or actual year-end results. The 2021/22 interval is an optimistic/cautious pupil scenario, not a confidence interval. The reported £74,368 support total combines £44,368 fundraising, £20,000 trust pledge and £10,000 parish council resolution. Do not label the total cash received or attribute every budget change solely to it.
- Exhibit 5: one longitudinal caution, Hazlewood; it does not estimate a repeat-proposal rate.
- Exhibit 6: an editorial priority order, without effectiveness scores, budgets, probabilities or claimed causal effects.
- Exhibit 7: four selected closure comparisons. Efforts, assessments and outcomes are documented separately; no tactic failure rate is calculated.
- Exhibit 8: online petition signature counts for all six original Isle of Wight schools, reported in paragraph 92 of the March 2025 Cabinet report. The online counts total 3,771. Paper counts are shown separately, never added to online counts because overlap is unknown. The snapshot relates to the initial autumn 2024 consultation, not final lifetime campaign totals. The outcome horizon is 31 August 2025. No adjustment is made for school size, campaign duration or signatory residence, and no effective threshold or causal effect can be identified.

The Hackney-wide 95% opposition figure is rounded from 207 of 219 clearly classifiable proposal-level responses. The process received 175 submissions; an individual could address several proposals. It is not 95% of 175 people, a De Beauvoir-only percentage, or a representative opinion poll. S25 sections 4.24-4.28 provide the denominator; S30 is the council's narrative summary.

## Reason coding

One analyst reviewed the source materials and coded six overlapping themes for each grouped episode. Each row records its sources and a coding explanation in `data/catalogue.json`.

- 2: an explicit ground in the decision or the adopted recommendation/rationale. A finding of 2 does not mean the factor caused success independently of other factors.
- 1: a matter was raised, considered, or part of the institutional route, but was not established as a ground for the favourable outcome.
- 0: not established in the reviewed record. It does not mean the factor was absent or ineffective.

No independent second coding was performed. Do not present coding as inter-rater-validated research. For the three Isle of Wight Cabinet reprieves, the minutes establish the outcomes but do not isolate a school-specific explanation. The matrix therefore records the shared discussion without inventing a decisive cause. St George's has no factor coded 2 because attributed reporting does not expose a sufficiently examined decision rationale. In St John the Divine's case, mixed-age classes and community provision were discussed but were not necessary to the adjudicator's central conclusion.

The matrix covers mechanisms and institutional circumstances, not merely campaign tactics. For example, rural status is not something Kew can acquire through campaign effort. Partner support can be a route to adjudication without constituting the merits on which a proposal was rejected.

## Evidence provenance

Eleven schools have primary decision/recommendation or judgment evidence; St George's has secondary reports quoting the trust. Fletching's proposed recommendation is paired with the council's later report confirming the 23 December 2019 decision. Pooles Park's High Court judgment was read through indexed text; direct retrieval was blocked. Its November 2023 ministerial decision is the catalogue's event date. Continued provision is verified through the current academy successor URN, not by treating the predecessor's administrative closure as lost provision.

The complete appendix lists all 45 sources used, including individual GIAS entries, with full URLs, publication/record dates, access dates, locators, inspection methods and claim IDs. The 49-entry ledger records case outcomes, observed efforts, follow-up, exhibits, contextual facts and editorial interpretations. Completeness means coverage of this pack, not every available source about these schools or all closure literature. Sources and claims are also supplied as JSON.

The register describes the consulted online versions; search-engine publication metadata was not substituted for dates printed within historical documents. Downloaded public-source PDFs and browser test intermediates are held outside the distributable package. The package includes original summaries, links, coding and the chart masters. Source URLs can change; recheck them before later publication.

## Limits on inference

Selection initially focused on favourable outcomes. Four purposively selected closure comparisons broaden the evidence but do not provide a national denominator, matched failed-campaign dataset, representative sampling frame or standard follow-up horizon. School type, geography, funding arrangements, date, reasons for closure and access to remedies differ. Different sources also report some issues much more fully than others. The presence of a tactic cannot establish that it increased the probability of success. The absence of a source mention cannot show that a tactic was unused.

So do not calculate campaign success odds, p-values, causal rankings or predicted returns on effort from this dataset. The valid use is to identify concrete hypotheses and evidence to test for Kew. To estimate a rate, first define a jurisdiction, period, entry stage and outcome horizon. Then gather all proposals, including closures, withdrawals, mergers, conversions, deferrals and unresolved cases. Preserve successor links and follow each case to the same horizon before calculating a denominator.

## Application to Kew Riverside Primary School

The proposal page retrieved on 22 September describes an initial/pre-statutory consultation. The current DfE closing-schools guidance applies from 1 September 2026. Historic legal processes should not be copied without checking present guidance and the school's type. Kew is a community school. Do not assume that a voluntary-aided governing body's or diocese's referral route gives every parent or community school a general appeal right. Do not assume that the rural-school presumption applies either.

The suggested priorities are a costed operating alternative and an audit of demand and net closure savings. They also include evidence of effects on families, formal participation and a specific process check where justified. The historical evidence does not show that any Kew alternative is already viable. School-specific budgets, partner commitments, pupil assumptions and continuing PFI obligations still need to be checked.
